core.description: Everything a character can do without knowing what it is holding: locomotion, crouch/sneak, jump, dodge, hit reactions, guard-break stagger, healing and death. Always loaded.

criticals.description: The riposte and backstab choreography, both roles. Shared by every melee weapon rather than duplicated per moveset, because the paired clips are the weapon-independent half of a critical.

oneHanded.description: Sword, axe and mace moveset: combat idle and crouch, the light and heavy chains, weapon guard and parry, draw and sheathe.

shield.description: Blocking behind a braced shield face rather than a weapon edge, plus the shield bash that serves as its parry. Loaded whenever something is in the off hand.

bow.description: The shooting cycle and bow-carry locomotion. Depends on the one-handed pack because a bow borrows that moveset for the clumsy bash it makes when swung — see the polish-backlog item about giving a bow its own melee, or none at all, so an archer stops downloading a sword's moveset for a fallback swing.

greatsword.description: Two-handed blade moveset (Skyrim's 2hm set): its own carriage, locomotion, chains, guard, parry and draw. The two-handed base every haft weapon also builds on.

greataxe.description: The heavier two-handed haft chains (Skyrim's 2hw set). Carriage, locomotion, guard and draw come from the greatsword pack, so only the swings differ.

pike.description: A pike's own two-handed thrusting moveset: idle, locomotion, the light chain, the power attacks, its guard and its draw. The parry, the criticals, run-back and crouch are not authored here; they come from the greatsword pack.

halberd.description: A halberd's own two-handed haft moveset: idle, the light chain, the power attacks, its guard and its draw. Locomotion, the parry and the criticals come from the `greataxe` (battleaxe and warhammer) and `greatsword` packs.

quarterstaff.description: A quarterstaff's own two-handed moveset: idle, the light chain, the power attacks, its guard and its draw. Locomotion, the parry and the criticals come from the `greataxe` (battleaxe and warhammer) and `greatsword` packs.

rapier.description: A rapier's own one-handed thrusting moveset: idle, the light chain, the power attacks and its draw. The guard, the parry, the criticals and all locomotion come from the one-handed pack.

claw.description: A claw fighter's own one-handed moveset: idle, the light chain, the power attacks and the block held without a blade. The guard entry, the draw, the parry, the criticals and all locomotion come from the one-handed pack.

katana.description: A katana's own one-handed moveset: drawn idle, the light chain, the power attacks, its guard and block-hits, its draw and its sprint. The parry, the criticals, the sheathe and the rest of the locomotion come from the one-handed pack. Every clip is converted from the mod's interleaved-uncompressed HKX by pipeline/hkx_interleaved.py.

dualWield.description: A second one-handed blade held in the left hand: the dual-wield drawn idle, the left-hand light cut, the left-hand forward power attack and the both-blades power attack. The right-hand attacks, guard, parry, criticals and locomotion come from the one-handed pack, as vanilla's 1hmdual animation set takes them.

torch.description: A torch held in the left hand: the torch-carrying arm pose (a single-frame left-arm overlay), and the torch guard's entry, held stance and block-hit. Attacks, parry, criticals and locomotion come from the one-handed pack, as vanilla's 1hmtorch animation set takes them.

source: Skyrim vanilla + permitted mod HKX (locally regenerated authorized runtime build)

IDLE.provenance: vanilla mt_idle_a_base (neutral unarmed standing idle, not a combat stance)

SWORD_IDLE.provenance: vanilla 1hm_idle (sword-drawn idle); separate action so IDLE/SWORD_IDLE swap independently

WALK_BACK.provenance: vanilla directional walk-back (real, not reversed forward)

RUN.provenance: vanilla male mt_runforward. Replaces 1hm_runforward, whose combat carriage holds both arms near the body: measured on the production rig its upper arms swing only 24/19 degrees against 88/79 degrees of thigh swing, which reads as shoulders bobbing with no arm swing. mt_runforward swings 43/35 degrees at the shoulder and 32/37 at the elbow over the identical stride.

SPRINT.provenance: vanilla male mt_sprintforward. mt_sprintforwardsword is the same sprint with the sword arm damped - measured on the production rig the two are identical on the left arm (49.2/50.8 degrees) and legs, and differ only on the right, which drops from 63.8 to 51.1 at the shoulder and 30.9 to 27.3 at the elbow. That asymmetry is exactly the reported 'left arm swings, right arm bobs'.

JUMP_START.provenance: vanilla mt_jump launch through source 0.5667s; exhaustive production-rig pose comparison selected a short 0.03s outgoing handoff into the continuation cut from mt_jumpfast; vertical COM stripped because the physics controller owns the jump arc

JUMP_IDLE.provenance: vanilla mt_jumpfast source 0.5667-0.8333, a sword-bearing continuation whose launch seam differs by at most 1.01 degrees on the audited production skeleton; fitted to the observed 0.20s airborne interval and clamped for longer falls without entering an authored landing; vertical COM stripped because the physics controller owns the jump arc

JUMP_LAND.provenance: vanilla stationary landing with a production-audited 0.18s entry blend and exact visible-surface contact

JUMP_LAND_LEFT.provenance: vanilla directional landing, left-foot transition with exact visible-surface contact

JUMP_LAND_RIGHT.provenance: vanilla directional landing, right-foot transition with exact visible-surface contact

ROLL.provenance: Dynamic Dodge Animation 1.5, DMCO 0.9.6 base OAR 6000 MCO_DodgeForward2.hkx; exhaustive weapon-mounted FOMOD/OAR audition retained this semantically correct one-handed tuck roll, fitted to a 0.64s authored-motion span so the exported leading pose and at least 0.055s of its clean upright endpoint both render inside the unchanged 0.72s gameplay lock; source frames 3 and 4 are an isolated left-hand quaternion spike that leaves and returns to its neighbours (70/20/100 degree steps between poses only 13.6 degrees apart), so both keys are removed declaratively and runtime slerp follows the untouched frame 2 and frame 5 neighbours; 120Hz visible-surface sampling protects the fast nonlinear tuck from between-keyframe floor penetration

BACKSTEP.provenance: vanilla Skyrim - Animations.bsa meshes/actors/character/animations/1hm_walkbackward.hkx, full guarded two-step retreat fitted exactly to the 0.52s gameplay lock; selected after exhaustive weapon-mounted review rejected Dynamic Dodge Backward1/TK StepDodgeBack as the same floaty hop and Backward2/TK DodgeBack as a somersault

GUARD_ENTER.provenance: vanilla one-handed sword block anticipate/guard entry. Its stance sits 0.174 m lower at the COM than the sword idle it blends from; now that both clips are correctly grounded that difference is real geometry rather than a hover, so the entry blend is lengthened to spread the support solve over more frames instead of stepping it in one.

GUARD_HIT_A.provenance: vanilla one-handed sword block-hit variant A

GUARD_HIT_B.provenance: vanilla one-handed sword block-hit variant B

PARRY.provenance: Rim Parry and Execution 1.1, OAR (9900433) one-handed sword block-bash intro; exact 9900433bb/1hm_blockbashintro.HKX catch, with short production-candidate entry/handoff blends so the 0.1667s authored catch remains readable

PARRY_FOLLOW_THROUGH.provenance: Rim Parry and Execution 1.1, OAR (9900433) one-handed sword block-bash follow-through; exact 9900433bb/1hm_blockbash.HKX deflection/recovery, with a production-candidate 0.14s return to combat idle

RIPOSTE.provenance: Rim Parry and Execution 1.1, one-handed sword execution attacker (2130000018)/1.hkx, CQC02 lunge selected from source 0.1667–1.3s; exhaustive production-paired review rejected the source 0.10s stray blade pass and established 0.1667s as the first robust anticipation frame, retaining the authored source 0.5667s contact and 0.7s withdrawal; production-audited 0.18s entry and 0.24s exit blends

GREATSWORD_RIPOSTE.provenance: Rim Parry and Execution 1.1, greatsword execution attacker (1Execution/(2130000022)greatsword/1.HKX). Trim and separation measured by scripts/measure-contact-windows.mjs --critical against the visual gate’s own measure: the blade passes 0.23 m from a victim’s spine at source 2.9750s with the pair 1.00 m apart. Earlier phases of the sequence only graze a shoulder.

GREATAXE_RIPOSTE.provenance: Rim Parry and Execution 1.1, battleaxe execution attacker (1Execution/(2130000023)waraxe/1.HKX). Contact measured at source 3.5083s with the pair 1.40 m apart, then moved 0.267s earlier: a battleaxe execution is an overhead, and the head reaches the victim on the way down rather than at its closest approach. The visual scenario measured that lead exactly (an unacknowledged contact beat), so the trim places the damage on the arrival instead.

BACKSTABBED_FORWARD.provenance: Rim Parry and Execution 1.1, OAR (6135054) "noshield hit back" forward stagger — the victim pitching forward from a blow in the back. The victim half of a two-handed backstab: the attacker plays its own weapon execution, which is what makes the critical weapon-specific, and this is the reaction to it. Weapon-independent on purpose — what being run through from behind does to you does not depend on what did it.
